---
title: "Create your personal workspace"
---

You only need to perform the complete procedure on this page once.

## 1. Sign in to GitHub

Open [GitHub](https://github.com/) and sign in with your personal account. If
you do not already have an account, create one before continuing.

### Recommended Codespaces setting

Before creating your first Codespace, open your GitHub account settings and
select **Codespaces**.

Set the **Default idle timeout** to **15 minutes**.

This is a course recommendation. It limits unnecessary use of your Codespaces
allowance if you forget to stop a session manually. You should still stop the
Codespace explicitly whenever you finish working.

## 2. Open the workspace template

Open the course workspace repository:

<https://github.com/gfulian/mineral-science-lab-workspace>

::: {.callout-warning}
## Do not fork the repository

Do **not** use **Fork** and do **not** select **Open in a codespace** directly
from the template.

You must first create your own repository from the template. This ensures that
your work is permanently connected to your own GitHub repository.
:::

## 3. Create your private repository

On the workspace template page:

1. Select **Use this template**.
2. Select **Create a new repository**.
3. Set **Owner** to your personal GitHub account.
4. Give the repository a recognizable name, for example
   `mineral-science-lab-yourname`.
5. Select **Private** visibility.
6. Leave **Include all branches** disabled.
7. Select **Create repository from template**.

You now have your own independent copy of the laboratory workspace.

Keep this repository private unless the instructor explicitly asks you to
change its visibility.

## 4. Create the Codespace

From **your new private repository**:

1. Select the green **Code** button.
2. Open the **Codespaces** tab.
3. Select **Create codespace on main**.

If GitHub offers a choice of machine type, select the **2-core** machine. The
laboratory notebook work does not require a larger machine.

The first initialization can take a few minutes. This is normal: GitHub is
creating the remote Linux environment and the course setup is installing the
required scientific Python packages.

::: {.callout-note}
## Wait for the setup to finish

During the first launch, a terminal may display package installation messages.
Wait until the setup reports:

```text
Environment ready.
```

before starting to work.
:::

## 5. Check the environment

Open a terminal inside the Codespace using **Terminal → New Terminal** and run:

```bash
python -c "import gemmi, spglib, numpy, scipy, pandas, matplotlib; print('Environment OK')"
```

The final line should be:

```text
Environment OK
```

Then check that the two course commands are available:

```bash
command -v update-course
command -v start-lab
```

Both commands should return a path.

You can also inspect the top-level directories:

```bash
ls
```

You should see, among other files:

```text
course
work
```

If these checks succeed, your laboratory environment is ready.

Continue with **[Working in Codespaces](03-working-in-codespaces.qmd)**.
